types.embedding_query_text: CommodityPrice: The monetary value of a commodity in the market Also called market price, resource price, raw material price. Examples: oil price, Fuel prices, food prices, crude oil price.

chosen_type.label: PriceSpecification
chosen_type.justification: PriceSpecification represents pricing details for offers, aligning with commodity prices in the market.

candidates.label: PriceSpecification
candidates.comment: A PriceSpecification is a StructuredValue representing a price or price range, typically used for markup of offers. Also called pricing details, cost specification. Examples: a product's list price, a service's hourly rate, a discount price, a price range for a flight. Distinct from MonetaryAmount, which describes independent amounts of money.

candidates.label: MonetaryAmount
candidates.comment: A structured value representing a monetary value or range, typically expressed with a currency. Also called amount of money, financial value, currency amount. Examples: "$50 USD", "£1,000 to £1,000,000 GBP", "€25.99". Distinct from PriceSpecification, which describes the price of an offer.

candidates.label: UnitPriceSpecification
candidates.comment: A structured value detailing the price asked for a specific offer by an organization or person. Also called price details, cost specification, offer price. Examples: "$10.99 per item", "€50 per hour", "£2.50 per unit".

candidates.label: CompoundPriceSpecification
candidates.comment: A price specification that combines multiple prices applicable for different dimensions of consumption. Also called bundled price, multi-component price, composite pricing. Examples: A utility bill with separate charges for electricity and water, a rental agreement with base rent and a "final cleaning" fee, a software license with per-user and per-feature costs. Distinct from PriceSpecification, which is a general description of a price.

candidates.label: DeliveryChargeSpecification
candidates.comment: A price specification detailing the cost associated with delivering an offer using a particular method. Also called Shipping cost, delivery fee, freight charge, postage cost. Examples: "Standard shipping: $5.99", "Express delivery: $15.00", "Free delivery for orders over $50". Distinct from DeliveryMethod, which describes the method itself, not its cost.

types.embedding_query_text: OilBenchmark: A standardized reference price for crude oil used globally Also called oil standard, crude benchmark, energy reference. Examples: Brent crude, global benchmark for oil.

chosen_type.label: OilBenchmark
chosen_type.definition: A standardized reference price for crude oil used globally
chosen_type.justification: No existing schema.org class matches the concept of an oil benchmark; PriceSpecification is the closest parent for pricing references.

candidates.label: EnergyEfficiencyEnumeration
candidates.comment: An EnergyEfficiencyEnumeration is an Enumeration of energy efficiency levels and certifications from various international standards. Also called energy rating, efficiency class, energy certification. Examples: EUEnergyEfficiencyEnumeration, EnergyStarEnergyEfficiencyEnumeration.

candidates.label: PriceSpecification
candidates.comment: A PriceSpecification is a StructuredValue representing a price or price range, typically used for markup of offers. Also called pricing details, cost specification. Examples: a product's list price, a service's hourly rate, a discount price, a price range for a flight. Distinct from MonetaryAmount, which describes independent amounts of money.

candidates.label: EnergyStarEnergyEfficiencyEnumeration
candidates.comment: An EnergyStarEnergyEfficiencyEnumeration is an EnergyEfficiencyEnumeration indicating whether a product is EnergyStar certified. Also called Energy Star rating, Energy Star certification. Examples: EnergyStarCertified, NotEnergyStarCertified.

candidates.label: ExchangeRateSpecification
candidates.comment: An ExchangeRateSpecification is a StructuredValue representing details about an exchange rate. Also called currency exchange rate, foreign exchange rate. Examples: The exchange rate between USD and EUR, a specific conversion rate for a financial transaction, details including fees and validity period.

candidates.label: EnergyConsumptionDetails
candidates.comment: EnergyConsumptionDetails is an Intangible providing information related to the energy efficiency of a product that consumes energy, based on international regulations. Also called energy efficiency data, power usage specifications, consumption metrics. Examples: A product's energy label showing kWh/year, details on standby power consumption, information on energy efficiency class.

types.embedding_query_text: GovernmentOfficial: A person holding an official position in government or military Also called public servant, state representative, military official. Examples: US ambassador to the UN, Iranian army spokesperson, Massimo Di Odoardo, United States ambassador to the UN.

chosen_type.label: GovernmentOfficial
chosen_type.definition: An individual holding a government position responsible for policy decisions.
chosen_type.justification: Candidates focus on organizations/services, not individuals; GovernmentOfficial as a subclass of Person fits the mentions.

candidates.label: GovernmentOffice
candidates.comment: A GovernmentOffice is a local business representing a specific governmental agency or department. Also called public agency office, state department branch, municipal service center. Examples: IRS office, DMV office, local planning department, social security office. Distinct from GovernmentBuilding, which is the physical structure that may contain multiple offices.

candidates.label: State
candidates.comment: A major administrative division of a country, such as a state or province. Also called province, region, territory, commonwealth. Examples: California, Ontario, Bavaria, Texas.

candidates.label: GovernmentOrganization
candidates.comment: A GovernmentOrganization is an organization or agency that is part of a governmental body. Also called public sector entity, state agency, governmental body. Examples: Department of Defense, Environmental Protection Agency, National Institutes of Health, local city council.

candidates.label: PostOffice
candidates.comment: A PostOffice is a GovernmentOffice providing postal services. Also called postal service branch, mail office. Examples: USPS Post Office, Royal Mail sorting office, a local post office branch, a general post office.

candidates.label: GovernmentService
candidates.comment: A GovernmentService is an intangible service provided by a government organization to the public. Also called public service, state-provided service, municipal offering. Examples: food stamps program, veterans benefits, public education, waste collection.

types.embedding_query_text: ShippingRoute: A designated path for maritime transportation of goods Also called maritime corridor, trade passage, transport route. Examples: Strait of Hormuz, Hormuz Strait, oil shipping route.

chosen_type.label: ShippingRoute
chosen_type.definition: A designated path for maritime transportation of goods
chosen_type.justification: GeoCoordinates is the only schema.org class for geographic data; ShippingRoute as a subclass fits the Strait of Hormuz example.

candidates.label: BoatTrip
candidates.comment: A Trip representing a journey taken on a commercial ferry line or similar water transport. Also called ferry journey, boat excursion, water travel. Examples: "A ferry trip across the English Channel", "A sightseeing boat trip on the river", "A commercial fishing boat trip". Distinct from BoatReservation, which is the booking for the trip.

candidates.label: ShippingService
candidates.comment: A structured value defining the criteria used to determine if and how an offer can be shipped to a customer. Also called delivery option, shipping method, freight service, courier choice. Examples: 'Standard Ground Shipping', 'Expedited Air Delivery', 'International Economy Shipping'.

candidates.label: TrainTrip
candidates.comment: A journey or itinerary undertaken using a commercial train line. Also called rail journey, train travel, railway trip. Examples: a cross-country train journey, a daily commute by train, a scenic train ride through the mountains.

candidates.label: ShippingRateSettings
candidates.comment: A structured value representing reusable shipping rate information, often linked to an offer via a shipping settings link. Also called shipping cost rules, freight pricing, delivery charges configuration. Examples: a flat rate shipping setting for standard delivery, a weight-based shipping rate table, a zone-based shipping cost.

candidates.label: BusTrip
candidates.comment: A BusTrip is a Trip taken on a commercial bus line. Also called bus journey, coach trip, bus travel. Examples: a cross-country bus journey, a daily commute by bus, a sightseeing bus tour.

types.embedding_query_text: Country Examples: Iran, US, Saudi Arabia, United States.

chosen_type.label: Country
chosen_type.justification: Country directly represents sovereign states, aligning with the mentions Iran, US, and Saudi Arabia.

candidates.label: Country
candidates.comment: A Country is a sovereign state or nation, representing a primary administrative division of the Earth's surface. Also called nation, state, sovereign state, realm. Examples: United States, Canada, France, Japan, Brazil.

candidates.label: ITNonprofitType
candidates.comment: ITNonprofitType is a nonprofit type enumeration specifically for non-profit organizations originating from Italy. Also called Italian non-profit category, Italy NPO type, Italian charity classification. Examples: 'ONLUS', 'APS', 'ODV' (specific Italian non-profit legal forms). Distinct from NonprofitType, which is a more general enumeration of non-profit organization types.

candidates.label: NLNonprofitType
candidates.comment: NLNonprofitType is an enumeration for specific non-profit organization types originating from the Netherlands. Also called Dutch non-profit type, Netherlands charity classification. Examples: ANBI (Algemeen Nut Beogende Instelling), SBBI (Sociaal Belang Behartigende Instelling). Distinct from NonprofitType, which is a general enumeration for non-profit types.

candidates.label: State
candidates.comment: A major administrative division of a country, such as a state or province. Also called province, region, territory, commonwealth. Examples: California, Ontario, Bavaria, Texas.

candidates.label: USNonprofitType
candidates.comment: An enumeration of specific non-profit organization types recognized within the United States. Also called US charity type, American non-profit category, US voluntary sector classification. Examples: a 501(c)(3) organization, a public charity, a private foundation.

types.embedding_query_text: MilitaryGroup: An organized armed faction operating within a region Also called armed organization, combat group, militia. Examples: Houthi militia in Yemen, Yemeni Houthi militia, Houthis.

chosen_type.label: MilitaryGroup
chosen_type.definition: An organization engaged in military activities or conflicts.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org class for military factions; Organization is the closest parent for structured groups.

candidates.label: PerformingGroup
candidates.comment: A PerformingGroup is an organization of performers, such as a band, orchestra, or circus. Also called performance ensemble, troupe, artistic group. Examples: Cirque du Soleil, a local theatre company, a dance troupe. Distinct from MusicGroup, which is specifically for musical performers.

candidates.label: MusicGroup
candidates.comment: A MusicGroup, as a PerformingGroup, is an organization of musicians, such as a band or orchestra, or a solo musician. Also called band, musical ensemble, orchestra, solo artist. Examples: The Beatles, New York Philharmonic, Taylor Swift. Distinct from PerformingGroup, which is a broader category for any performance group.

candidates.label: TheaterGroup
candidates.comment: An organization or company dedicated to producing and performing theatrical works. Also called theater company, drama troupe, acting ensemble. Examples: The Royal Shakespeare Company, Cirque du Soleil, a local amateur dramatics society.

candidates.label: SearchRescueOrganization
candidates.comment: An organization dedicated to finding and providing aid to people who are lost or in imminent danger. Also called SAR team, rescue service, emergency search unit. Examples: a mountain rescue team, a coast guard search and rescue unit, a volunteer SAR group.

candidates.label: DanceGroup
candidates.comment: A DanceGroup is a performing organization specializing in dance, often presenting choreographed performances. Also called dance company, ballet troupe, dance ensemble, dance collective. Examples: Alvin Ailey American Dance Theater, Riverdance, New York City Ballet, Bolshoi Ballet.

chosen_type.label: SeaBodyOfWater
chosen_type.justification: Red Sea is a saltwater body, fitting SeaBodyOfWater's description of seas/oceans.

candidates.label: GeoCoordinates
candidates.comment: GeoCoordinates is a StructuredValue representing the geographic coordinates of a place or event, typically latitude and longitude. Also called geographic location, GPS coordinates, spatial coordinates. Examples: Latitude 34.0522, Longitude -118.2437 (for Los Angeles), a specific point on a map, the coordinates of an event venue.

candidates.label: SeaBodyOfWater
candidates.comment: A large expanse of saltwater, typically part of an ocean or a large inland body of saltwater. Also called sea, ocean, marine body, saltwater expanse. Examples: the Mediterranean Sea, the Caribbean Sea, the Black Sea, the Caspian Sea. Distinct from RiverBodyOfWater, which is a flowing freshwater course.

candidates.label: OceanBodyOfWater
candidates.comment: An OceanBodyOfWater, as a BodyOfWater, is a large expanse of saltwater, such as the Pacific Ocean. Also called ocean, sea, marine body. Examples: Atlantic Ocean, Indian Ocean, Southern Ocean. Distinct from LakeBodyOfWater, which is an inland freshwater body.

candidates.label: BoatTerminal
candidates.comment: A CivicStructure serving as a station for boats, ships, and other water vessels to dock and embark/disembark passengers or cargo. Also called ferry terminal, cruise port, marina, dock. Examples: "The Seattle Ferry Terminal", "PortMiami cruise terminal", "A local marina office".

candidates.label: VirtualLocation
candidates.comment: An online or non-physical location where events can be attended, such as a webinar or online meeting. Also called online venue, remote location, digital space. Examples: a Zoom meeting room, a webinar platform, a virtual conference hall.

types.embedding_query_text: EnergyStorage: Capacity to store energy resources for future use Also called fuel reserves, energy capacity, storage infrastructure. Examples: European gas storage.

chosen_type.label: EnergyStorage
chosen_type.definition: Capacity to store energy resources for future use
chosen_type.justification: Energy is the only schema.org class for energy-related quantities; EnergyStorage as a subclass fits the context.

candidates.label: SelfStorage
candidates.comment: A local business providing rental units for individuals and businesses to store their belongings. Also called storage facility, mini-storage, public storage. Examples: 'U-Haul Self-Storage', 'Extra Space Storage', 'Local Storage Units'.

candidates.label: GasStation
candidates.comment: A GasStation is an AutomotiveBusiness that sells fuel for vehicles. Also called petrol station, filling station, service station. Examples: Shell, ExxonMobil, a local independent gas station.

candidates.label: ConvenienceStore
candidates.comment: A local business retail store offering a limited range of everyday items, often with extended hours. Also called corner store, mini-mart, quick shop. Examples: 7-Eleven, Circle K, a local neighborhood market, a gas station store. Distinct from Store, which is a general retail establishment.

candidates.label: Energy
candidates.comment: As a Quantity, Energy represents a numerical value combined with a unit of energy. Also called power, work, heat. Examples: "100 kWh", "500 Joules", "200 Calories", "1.21 Gigawatts".

candidates.label: EUEnergyEfficiencyEnumeration
candidates.comment: An EUEnergyEfficiencyEnumeration is an EnergyEfficiencyEnumeration listing the EU energy efficiency classes A-G, A+, A++, and A+++ as defined in EU directive 2017/1369. Also called EU energy rating, European energy class. Examples: EUEnergyEfficiencyCategoryA, EUEnergyEfficiencyCategoryA+++, EUEnergyEfficiencyCategoryG.

types.embedding_query_text: CentralBank: A financial institution overseeing a nation's monetary system Also called monetary authority, bank regulator, financial institution. Examples: Bank of England, European Central Bank, BoE, UK central bank.

chosen_type.label: BankOrCreditUnion
chosen_type.justification: Central banks are financial institutions; BankOrCreditUnion is the closest schema.org class for such entities.

candidates.label: BankOrCreditUnion
candidates.comment: A FinancialService provided by an institution that handles money and credit for customers. Also called bank, credit union, financial institution. Examples: "Chase Bank", "Navy Federal Credit Union", "Citibank". Distinct from AutomatedTeller, which is a machine, not an institution.

candidates.label: MonetaryAmount
candidates.comment: A structured value representing a monetary value or range, typically expressed with a currency. Also called amount of money, financial value, currency amount. Examples: "$50 USD", "£1,000 to £1,000,000 GBP", "€25.99". Distinct from PriceSpecification, which describes the price of an offer.

candidates.label: FinancialService
candidates.comment: A FinancialService is a LocalBusiness that provides financial services. Also called bank, credit union, investment firm, insurance company. Examples: A retail bank, a wealth management firm, an insurance agency, a loan provider.

candidates.label: BankAccount
candidates.comment: A FinancialProduct or service offered by a bank for depositing, withdrawing, or transferring money, often with interest. Also called bank account, checking account, savings account, deposit account. Examples: "My personal checking account", "A business savings account", "A joint current account".

candidates.label: AutomatedTeller
candidates.comment: A FinancialService provided by a machine for banking transactions. Also called ATM, cash machine, automated banking machine. Examples: "Bank of America ATM", "Wells Fargo cash machine", "independent ATM kiosk".

types.embedding_query_text: EconomicIndicator: A measurable macroeconomic statistic used to assess economic health Also called economic metric, financial indicator, market statistic. Examples: inflation rate.

chosen_type.label: EconomicIndicator
chosen_type.definition: An indicator representing the economic status or value of a commodity, such as oil prices.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org class for economic indicators; Thing is the broadest applicable parent.

candidates.label: MedicalRiskScore
candidates.comment: A medical risk estimator that is a simple system summing risk factors to yield a score associated with prognosis. Also called clinical score, prognostic score, risk index. Examples: "CHAD score", "TIMI risk score", "APACHE II score". Distinct from MedicalRiskCalculator, which involves more complex mathematical calculations.

candidates.label: MedicalRiskCalculator
candidates.comment: A medical risk estimator that is a complex mathematical calculation, often requiring an online tool, used to assess prognosis. Also called prognosis calculator, risk assessment tool, clinical prediction model. Examples: a calculator for cardiovascular disease risk, a tool for predicting cancer recurrence. Distinct from MedicalRiskScore, which is a simpler sum of risk factors.

candidates.label: MedicalRiskEstimator
candidates.comment: A medical entity representing any rule set or interactive tool used to estimate the risk of developing a complication or condition. Also called risk assessment tool, prognosis predictor, clinical risk model. Examples: a calculator for stroke risk, a scoring system for surgical complications. Distinct from MedicalRiskFactor, which is a single factor increasing risk.

candidates.label: FinancialIncentive
candidates.comment: A FinancialIncentive is an Intangible representing financial benefits offered for goods or services, including details like amount, status, and eligibility criteria. Also called rebate, subsidy, grant, discount. Examples: A government tax credit for electric vehicles, a manufacturer's rebate on an appliance, a low-interest loan program, a student scholarship.

candidates.label: MedicalIndication
candidates.comment: A medical entity representing a condition or factor that suggests the use of a medical therapy. Also called indication for treatment, therapeutic rationale, medical justification. Examples: "high blood pressure" as an indication for antihypertensive drugs, "fever" as an indication for antipyretics.

types.embedding_query_text: InterestRate: The percentage charged for borrowing or invested capital Also called rate of interest, borrowing cost, financial rate. Examples: 3.75%.

chosen_type.label: LoanOrCredit
chosen_type.justification: Interest rates are part of loan terms; LoanOrCredit is the most relevant schema.org class.

candidates.label: LoanOrCredit
candidates.comment: A financial product representing an amount of money loaned or a line of credit offered under specific terms and charges. Also called credit facility, lending product, financial loan. Examples: a personal loan, a credit card, a mortgage, a business line of credit. Distinct from MortgageLoan, which is specifically a loan secured by real estate.

candidates.label: RepaymentSpecification
candidates.comment: A RepaymentSpecification is a StructuredValue representing the details of a repayment. Also called repayment terms, loan repayment details, amortization schedule. Examples: a mortgage repayment schedule, the terms for a credit card payment, details of a student loan repayment plan, a payment installment plan.

candidates.label: MortgageLoan
candidates.comment: A loan or credit product where property or real estate is used as collateral. Also called home loan, property loan, real estate financing. Examples: a 30-year fixed-rate mortgage, a variable-rate home loan, a commercial property mortgage. Distinct from LoanOrCredit, which is a general loan and not necessarily secured by real estate.

candidates.label: MonetaryAmount
candidates.comment: A structured value representing a monetary value or range, typically expressed with a currency. Also called amount of money, financial value, currency amount. Examples: "$50 USD", "£1,000 to £1,000,000 GBP", "€25.99". Distinct from PriceSpecification, which describes the price of an offer.

candidates.label: BankAccount
candidates.comment: A FinancialProduct or service offered by a bank for depositing, withdrawing, or transferring money, often with interest. Also called bank account, checking account, savings account, deposit account. Examples: "My personal checking account", "A business savings account", "A joint current account".

types.embedding_query_text: ResearchOrganization: An institution conducting specialized studies and analyses Also called analytical firm, study group, research institute. Examples: Wood Mackenzie.

chosen_type.label: ResearchOrganization
chosen_type.justification: ResearchOrganization directly matches the definition of an institution conducting specialized studies.

candidates.label: ResearchOrganization
candidates.comment: A ResearchOrganization is an Organization dedicated to conducting research. Also called scientific institute, research company, academic research center. Examples: Max Planck Society, Bell Labs, a university research department, a pharmaceutical research firm.

candidates.label: ArchiveOrganization
candidates.comment: An ArchiveOrganization is a LocalBusiness that maintains, preserves, and typically provides public access to archival materials. Also called archives, historical society, records center, repository. Examples: National Archives, a university special collections library, a corporate archive, a local historical society.

candidates.label: EducationalOrganization
candidates.comment: An EducationalOrganization is a CivicStructure that provides education. Also called learning institution, academic body, school. Examples: A university, a high school, a vocational college, a research institute.

candidates.label: SportsOrganization
candidates.comment: A general category for organizations involved in sports, including teams, governing bodies, and associations. Also called athletic organization, sports body, sports group. Examples: the NBA, a local youth soccer league, the International Olympic Committee.

candidates.label: MedicalOrganization
candidates.comment: An organization, physical or virtual, operating in the medical domain, such as a hospital or clinic. Also called healthcare organization, medical institution, health system. Examples: "Mayo Clinic", "World Health Organization", "Doctors Without Borders". Distinct from Organization, which is a broader category for any group.

chosen_type.label: Date
chosen_type.definition: A calendar date without time component, representing a temporal marker for events.
chosen_type.justification: Date is a schema.org datatype for calendar dates, fitting the examples like '2026-07-27'.

candidates.label: Date
candidates.comment: Date is a data type representing a specific calendar date, typically formatted according to ISO 8601. Also called calendar date, specific day. Examples: "2023-10-27", "1999-12-31", "0001-01-01".

candidates.label: DayOfWeek
candidates.comment: An enumeration representing a specific day of the week, used for scheduling or recurring events. Also called Weekday, calendar day, day name. Examples: Monday, Tuesday, Saturday, Sunday. Distinct from Date, which specifies a particular calendar date.

candidates.label: ShippingDeliveryTime
candidates.comment: A structured value providing details about the expected delivery times for product shipping. Also called delivery timeframe, estimated delivery, shipping lead time, transit time. Examples: 'ships in 1-2 business days', 'delivery by Friday', 'estimated 3-5 day transit'.

candidates.label: DateTime
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, combining both date and time components according to ISO 8601. Also called Timestamp, date and time string, ISO 8601 datetime. Examples: "2023-10-27T10:30:00Z", "1999-12-31T23:59:59-05:00", "2024-01-15T14:00:00". Distinct from Date, which only specifies a calendar date without time.

candidates.label: EventAttendanceModeEnumeration
candidates.comment: An EventAttendanceModeEnumeration is an Enumeration of modes for organizing an event, indicating whether it is online or offline. Also called attendance type, event format, participation mode. Examples: OnlineEventAttendanceMode, OfflineEventAttendanceMode, MixedEventAttendanceMode.
